author: TradingCalc
description: 91 deterministic tools across options, forex, quant risk/stats, prediction markets, on-chain safety, and crypto futures: Deribit BTC/ETH options (options_payoff, black_scholes, black_scholes_live, straddle_strangle, covered_call_protective_put, implied_volatility), forex (pip value, margin level, breakeven, pnl, risk/reward, scenario, average entry, position size, margin required, currency converter, swap/rollover cost, correlation - manual + live-FX-rate variants), risk/stats (var_cvar, sharpe_stats, hurst_exponent, cointegration, portfolio_tearsheet, garch, risk_parity, dsr, kelly_frontier, unsmoothing, evt_tail_risk, orderbook_impact), prediction markets across Kalshi, Polymarket, Limitless, Myriad and ADI Predictstreet's crypto categories (odds_converter, market_implied_odds, prediction_market_edge, window_fair_value, spread_reader), chain-agnostic on-chain (token_risk_check, swap_price_impact, bonding_curve on Solana; market_cap_comparison and wallet_flag_check on Solana + 5 EVM chains), trade planning (pnl, breakeven, exit_target, scenario, dca_entry, scale_out), risk (liquidation, position_sizing, max_leverage, risk_reward), funding & carry (funding_cost, funding_arb, compound_funding, funding_breakeven, carry_trade), market structure (open_analysis, session_structure, value_migration, breakout_acceptance), crypto spot (crypto_profit), cross-exchange price agreement (price_consensus), primitives (average_entry, hedge_ratio), and integrated decision (pre_trade_check, portfolio_risk). Formulas normalized across 17 exchanges, linear and inverse contracts. Every response signed with ECDSA P-256. Not AI estimates, exact numbers your trading bot can trust.
name: tradingcalc-mcp

tools.name: workflow.run_pnl_planning
tools.title: PnL Planning
tools.description: Calculate net PnL, ROE, fees and gross profit/loss for a futures trade. Use when user asks "what's my profit/loss on this trade?" Returns: grossPnl, fees, netPnl, netPnlUsdt, roe (%), maxLossBound (only non-null for an inverse/coin-margined short: the finite ceiling on net coin-denominated loss as price rises without limit, (size/entryPrice)×(1+feeOpenPct) - includes the opening fee, since it survives the exit-price-to-infinity limit while the closing fee vanishes - null for every other side/contractType combination, which either has no such bound or a trivial one).

size.description: Position size: base asset qty for linear, USD contracts for inverse

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, pnl/fees are returned in the base coin, not USDT.

tools.name: workflow.run_liquidation_safety
tools.title: Liquidation Safety
tools.description: Calculate the liquidation price for an isolated-margin futures position with one flat maintenance margin rate (mmr, which you supply from your exchange's tier). It is a generic flat-rate model, for linear and inverse alike, not any one exchange's engine. By default the maintenance margin is taken on the position value at the liquidation price (the form Bybit, KuCoin and Hyperliquid document); mmBase "entry" takes it on the entry value (the form MEXC documents); liqFeeRate adds a liquidation fee to the rate (KuCoin). No tiered maintenance amounts, no extra margin, no cross-margin (shared collateral) logic, so it does not apply to cross-margin accounts and can differ from an exchange's own figure. Use when user asks "where will I get liquidated?" or "how close is my liq price?". Returns: liqPrice (the price). liqPrice is null when the position cannot be liquidated: an inverse short whose margin covers any price rise (at 1x or less with the default mmBase; with mmBase "entry" only a little below 1x). Check for null before doing arithmetic on it.

mmBase.description: Value the maintenance margin is taken on: "liquidation" = position value at the liquidation price (default; Bybit, KuCoin, Hyperliquid), "entry" = entry value (MEXC).

liqFeeRate.description: Liquidation fee as a fraction of position value, default 0, max 0.05; added to mmr (e.g. KuCoin 0.0006).

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined (e.g. Deribit/Bybit/MEXC BTC-settled perps).

tools.name: workflow.run_breakeven_planning
tools.title: Breakeven Planning
tools.description: Calculate the break-even exit price that covers all trading fees: this alone, nothing else. Use when user asks only "what price do I need to just break even?" and nothing more. If the user also gave a stop/target or wants a full trade-safety check, use workflow.run_risk_reward or workflow.run_pre_trade_check instead; both already include this breakeven figure plus more. Returns: breakevenPrice, totalFees.

sizeBase.description: Position size: base asset qty for linear, USD contracts for inverse

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, totalFees is returned in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_position_sizing
tools.title: Position Sizing
tools.description: Calculate the correct position size given a maximum risk in USDT and a stop-loss price. Use when user asks "how many coins should I buy?" or "size my position so I risk exactly $X". Returns: positionSize (base), positionUsdt, marginRequired.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, sizeQuote is USD contracts and margin is returned in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_funding_cost
tools.title: Funding Cost
tools.description: Calculate the total funding cost (or income) for holding a perpetual futures position. Use when user asks "how much funding will I pay holding X days?" or "is funding eating my profit?". Returns: totalCost (positive = you pay, negative = you receive; in the coin for inverse), costPerDay, annualPct, totalPeriods, breakevenShift (size of the price move whose PnL equals the funding: up for a positive rate, down for a negative one, for either side).

fundingRate.description: Funding rate per funding interval as a fraction, e.g. 0.0001 (per 8h unless intervalHours says otherwise)

intervalHours.description: Hours between funding payments, which is the period fundingRate covers. Default 8 (3 payments a day); 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack, 4 or 2 on some symbols of Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, MEXC, Aster and Phemex.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, sizeBase is USD contracts and cost figures come out in the base coin.

tools.name: primitive.average_entry
tools.title: Average Entry Price
tools.description: Calculate the weighted average entry price from multiple buy/sell fills (DCA): the bare number only, no breakeven or per-fill breakdown. Use when user asks only "what's my average entry?" and wants just that figure. Each fill is { price, quantity } here (workflow.run_dca_entry calls the same field size). For breakeven and a per-level summary too, use workflow.run_dca_entry instead. Returns: averagePrice, totalSize, totalCost.

fills.description: Buy/sell fills to average, each with a price and a quantity (at least 1)

quantity.description: Fill quantity, required unless "size" is given (the same field)

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined, average is the arithmetic mean (default). inverse = coin-margined, average is the harmonic mean (fill quantity is USD notional).

tools.name: workflow.run_exit_target
tools.title: Exit Target
tools.description: Calculate the exact exit price needed to hit a target PnL or ROE percentage. Use when user asks "at what price do I take profit to make $500?" or "where should I set TP for 20% ROE?". Returns: targetExitPrice.

targetValue.description: Target value (USDT/coin for pnl mode, or %)

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, pnl-mode targetValue and outputs are in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_scenario_planning
tools.title: Scenario Planning
tools.description: Run a scenario analysis: compute PnL for multiple price-change percentages at once. Use when user asks "show me my P&L if BTC moves -10%, -5%, +5%, +10%". Returns: array of { deltaPct, exitPrice, netPnl, roe }.

deltasPct.description: List of price change percentages, e.g. [-10, -5, 0, 5, 10]. Must be at least -100 (exactly -100 only for linear contracts; inverse contracts need more than -100)

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. For inverse, size is USD contracts and pnl/fees come out in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_max_leverage
tools.title: Max Leverage
tools.description: Calculate the maximum leverage that keeps a position within a drawdown limit, from account size, max acceptable drawdown, and asset daily volatility. Use when user asks "what leverage does a 10% drawdown limit allow on BTC?" or "what leverage fits a 3% daily volatility and a 10% drawdown limit?". Returns: maxLeverage (maxDrawdownPct / (volatilityPct + mmr x 100), rounded down to 0.1, never below 1x), marginAtRisk (accountSize x maxDrawdownPct / 100, in USDT), safeMargin (USDT) and liquidationBuffer (percent). maxDrawdownPct and volatilityPct are percents (10 means 10%); mmr is a fraction (0.005 is 0.5%).

maxDrawdownPct.description: Maximum acceptable drawdown as percentage, e.g. 10 for 10%

volatilityPct.description: Expected daily price volatility as percentage, e.g. 3 for 3%

tools.name: primitive.hedge_ratio
tools.title: Hedge Ratio
tools.description: Calculate the short perpetual futures position size needed to hedge a spot holding. Default USDT-linear: sizes and costs in USD. With contractType "inverse" (coin-margined, needs entryPrice) the short is the same USD contracts and margin and funding come back in the base coin. Use when user asks "how much should I short to hedge my BTC?" or "what margin do I need for a 100% hedge?". Returns: perpNotional, requiredMargin, dailyFundingCost, annualFundingCost, hedgeCoverage, contractType and costUnit ("USD", or "base_coin" for inverse: read it before showing margin or funding as dollars). Inverse converts at the one entryPrice you give, so the coin figures assume the price stays there.

hedgeRatio.description: Percentage of spot to hedge, e.g. 100 for full hedge, 50 for half. Default 100.

leverage.description: Leverage on the perp short. Default 1.

fundingRatePct.description: Current funding rate per funding interval as a percentage, e.g. 0.01 (per 8h unless intervalHours says otherwise). Used for cost estimate.

intervalHours.description: Hours between funding payments, the period fundingRatePct covers. Default 8 (3 payments a day); 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack (per-hour rates); 4 or 2 on some symbols of Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, MEXC, Aster and Phemex.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default). inverse = coin-margined: spotSize stays the USD value of the holding, requiredMargin and the funding costs are returned in the base coin.

entryPrice.description: Coin price in USD. Required for contractType inverse (converts the USD margin and funding to coin); ignored for linear.

tools.name: workflow.run_funding_arbitrage
tools.title: Funding Arbitrage
tools.description: Calculate funding rate arbitrage profit: annualized yield, net profit, and breakeven days for a long/short basis trade across two exchanges: the bare numbers only, no plain-English verdict. For the same math plus a profitable/marginal/loss verdict, use workflow.run_carry_trade instead. Use when user asks "is this funding arb worth it?" or "how many days to break even on transfer fees?". Returns: netProfitUsdt, annualizedYieldPct, breakevenDays.

longFundingRate.description: Funding rate on long side (% per interval, positive = you pay)

shortFundingRate.description: Funding rate on short side (% per interval, positive = you receive)

transferFeePct.description: One-time transfer/setup fee as percentage, e.g. 0.1 for 0.1%

intervalHours.description: Hours between funding payments, one interval for both legs. Default 8; 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack (per-hour rates); 4 or 2 on some symbols. A leg paid on another interval is entered as its rate times (this interval / its own interval).

tools.name: workflow.run_compound_funding
tools.title: Compound Funding
tools.description: Project capital growth from reinvesting perpetual futures funding income (compounding carry). Use when user asks "how much will I make compounding 0.01% funding for 90 days?" or "what's my APY on this carry position?". Funding received is split by reinvestPct (the rest is withdrawn and still counts as earned); funding paid comes out of capital in full, and the capital never goes below 0. Returns: finalCapital, totalWithdrawn, endValue, totalEarned, totalEarnedPct, annualizedAPY, dailyEarnings, snapshots.

fundingRatePct.description: Funding rate per interval as percentage, e.g. 0.01 for 0.01%

intervalHours.description: Hours between funding payments, the period fundingRatePct covers, a whole number of hours that divides 24. Default 8; 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack (per-hour rates); 4 or 2 on some symbols.

durationDays.description: Number of days to project, up to 3650

reinvestPct.description: Percentage of funding received that is reinvested each interval, 0-100 (the rest is withdrawn and counts as earned; funding paid always comes out of capital). 100 = full compounding. Default 100.

tools.name: workflow.run_pre_trade_check
tools.title: Pre Trade Check
tools.description: Full pre-trade decision card: orchestrates position sizing, breakeven, liquidation, and funding cost in one call. Use when user describes a full trade setup and asks "should I take this trade?" or "run the numbers on this setup". Provide exchange+symbol to fetch live funding rate automatically. For an R:R-graded verdict on an entry, stop and target, see workflow.run_risk_reward. Returns: positionSize, breakeven, liquidationPrice, fundingCost, overnightBreakevenShift, verdict. liquidation_price and the liquidation distance are null when the position cannot be liquidated (an inverse short at 1x or less): check for null before using them.

exchange.description: Exchange code, e.g. "binance" or "bybit". Used to fetch the live funding rate if funding_rate is omitted, and to set funding_interval_hours when that is omitted (1 for Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack, whose rates are per hour; pass funding_interval_hours: 8 if you supply a rate that is per 8 hours). With funding_rate omitted and fetched live, funding_interval_hours is ignored and the interval the exchange reports for the symbol is used.

funding_rate.description: Funding rate per funding interval as decimal, e.g. 0.0001. If omitted, fetched live from exchange.

funding_interval_hours.description: Hours per funding payment, the period funding_rate covers: 8 on most venues, 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack, 4 or 2 on some symbols of Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, MEXC, Aster and Phemex. When funding_rate is omitted and fetched live (exchange and symbol given), any value passed here is ignored: the interval of that symbol as the exchange reports it is used (else the exchange default). Omitted otherwise: when you pass funding_rate yourself, the exchange default (1 for hourly venues, else 8), so pass funding_interval_hours for a symbol that pays every 4 or 2 hours.

hold_hours.description: Expected hold time in hours for overnight shift calc. Default 8.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined (e.g. Bybit BTCUSD). All returned figures (notional, margin, risk_amount, funding_cost_*) stay USD-denominated either way; recommended_size is USD notional (contracts) for inverse.

tools.name: workflow.run_risk_reward
tools.title: Risk Reward
tools.description: Full risk:reward analysis: takes a trade with entry, stop, AND target (all three). Calculates R:R ratio, position size, liquidation price, breakeven, and P&L at both stop and target. Returns a verdict label, strong (3:1+) / good (2:1+) / marginal / poor, which grades the R:R ratio against fixed thresholds and is not a recommendation. For a full setup check tied to a live exchange/symbol (including funding cost), see workflow.run_pre_trade_check; its verdict covers overall setup safety, not just R:R. Use when user asks "what's my risk reward on this setup?" or "what R:R do this entry, stop and target give?". liquidation_price and the liquidation distance are null when the position cannot be liquidated (an inverse short at 1x or less): check for null before using them.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined (e.g. Bybit BTCUSD). position_size/notional are USD notional (contracts) for inverse; pnl_at_stop/pnl_at_target come back denominated in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_portfolio_risk
tools.title: Portfolio Risk
tools.description: Aggregates risk across multiple open positions in one call: total notional, total P&L, total margin in use, margin usage as a % of account balance (if given), and which single position sits closest to liquidation. Each position is computed through the same canonical PnL/liquidation math as the single-position tools, then rolled up. Linear (USDT-margined) positions sum into one USD total; inverse (coin-margined) positions are grouped by settlement coin instead, since a BTC-margined P&L cannot be summed with an ETH-margined one without a live conversion rate. Returns a verdict label, healthy / watch / reduce / critical, which places the closest liquidation distance and margin usage in fixed bands and is not a recommendation. Use when user asks "how exposed am I across all my positions?" or "which of my positions is closest to liquidation?". Position size follows the product-wide convention: base-asset quantity for linear, USD notional (contracts) for inverse. liquidation_price and liq_distance_pct of a position are null when it cannot be liquidated (an inverse short at 1x or less); the closest liquidation skips it.

positions.description: Open positions to aggregate (1 to 50). Each: { side, entry_price, mark_price, size, leverage }, plus optional fees, mmr, contractType, coin, label.

label.description: Optional label to identify this position in the response (defaults to "Position N")

size.description: Position size: base-asset quantity for linear, USD notional (contracts) for inverse

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined (e.g. Bybit BTCUSD)

coin.description: Settlement coin, required when contractType is inverse (e.g. "BTC", "ETH")

account_balance.description: Optional account balance in USD, used to compute margin_usage_pct: linear margin plus every inverse position's own margin marked to market at its mark_price, all as one USD total

tools.name: workflow.run_dca_entry
tools.title: DCA Entry
tools.description: DCA entry planner: weighted average entry price, breakeven, and per-level contribution from multiple fill prices and sizes. Each fill is { price, size } here (primitive.average_entry calls the same field quantity). Compared with primitive.average_entry, this one adds output for the case where breakeven or the per-level breakdown is also wanted, not just the bare average. Use when user bought at several prices and asks "what's my average entry?" or "where is my DCA breakeven?". Returns: averageEntry, breakeven, per-level summary.

entries.description: Fills to average (2 to 20). Each: { price, size }, e.g. [{ "price": 60000, "size": 0.5 }, { "price": 58000, "size": 1 }]. Size is base-asset quantity for linear, USD notional (contracts) for inverse.

size.description: Fill size, required unless "quantity" is given (the same field)

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. Each fill's size is USD notional (contracts) for inverse; averageEntry is then the harmonic mean of fill prices, not the arithmetic mean.

tools.name: workflow.run_average_down
tools.title: Average Down
tools.description: Should-I-average-down check: for an already-open position, compares adding more at a worse price against the always-available alternative of buying the same final total size fresh at today's price. Returns the new blended average entry, liquidation price and breakeven (before vs. after), margin_added (the actual cash/margin required for the add at this leverage, not the full notional), and three risk figures at your stop-loss: existing_risk (what you already risk, before adding), pyramid_risk (what you'd risk after adding), and clean_entry_risk (what a fresh entry at add_price for the same total size would risk). risk_penalty_pct is how much MORE than that fresh-entry alternative you're risking - for any genuine average-down (add_price worse than existing_entry_price) pyramid_risk is provably always greater than clean_entry_risk. liquidation_before_stop is true when the new liquidation price sits at or beyond your own stop-loss, meaning the exchange would force-close the position before the stop-loss ever triggers. Use when user asks "should I add to this losing position?" or "what does averaging down actually cost me here?". liquidation_price and the liquidation distance are null when the position cannot be liquidated (an inverse short at 1x or less): check for null before using them.

existing_entry_price.description: Entry price of the position already held

existing_size.description: Size already held: base-asset quantity for linear, USD notional (contracts) for inverse

add_price.description: Proposed price to add at - also treated as today's current price for the fresh-entry comparison

add_size.description: Additional size being considered, same unit convention as existing_size

stop_loss.description: Stop-loss price (must be below add_price for a long, above it for a short - the position should already be closed otherwise)

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. Risk figures come back denominated in the base coin for inverse.

tools.name: workflow.run_scale_out
tools.title: Scale Out
tools.description: Scale-out planner: P&L, ROI, and cumulative P&L for each partial exit level. Use when user wants to take profit at multiple targets: "close 30% at $90k, 30% at $95k, 40% at $100k, what's my total P&L?". Returns: per-level pnl, weightedAvgExitPrice, totalRoi.

total_size.description: Total position size in base currency

exits.description: Partial exit levels (2 to 10). Each: { price, pct }, e.g. [{ "price": 90000, "pct": 30 }, { "price": 95000, "pct": 70 }]; the pct values must not sum to more than 100.

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. total_size is USD notional (contracts) for inverse, and per-level pnl comes back denominated in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_carry_trade
tools.title: Carry Trade
tools.description: Delta-neutral carry trade (funding arbitrage) analysis, with a profitable/marginal/loss verdict on top of the same math primitive.funding_arb uses. Compared with primitive.funding_arb, this one adds output for the case where a plain-English verdict is wanted, not just the raw numbers. Use when user asks "is this carry trade worth it?": long on exchange A, short on exchange B, collect the funding rate spread. Returns: netYieldPct, grossProfit, netProfit, breakevenDays, verdict (profitable/marginal/loss).

funding_rate_long.description: Funding rate on long exchange per interval (decimal)

funding_rate_short.description: Funding rate on short exchange per interval (decimal)

interval_hours.description: Hours between funding payments, one interval for both legs (default 8; 1 for hourly venues; 4 or 2 on some symbols). A leg paid on another interval is entered as its rate times (this interval / its own interval).

tools.name: workflow.run_funding_breakeven
tools.title: Funding Breakeven
tools.description: Price move needed to cover funding cost + fees over a holding period. Use when user asks "how much does BTC need to move for me to profit after funding?" or "is funding killing my edge on this trade?". Returns: breakevenWithFunding, breakevenWithoutFunding, requiredMovePct.

funding_rate.description: Funding rate per funding interval (decimal, e.g. 0.0001)

funding_interval_hours.description: Hours per funding payment, the period funding_rate covers: 8 (default), 1 on Hyperliquid, dYdX, Kraken and Backpack (per-hour rates), 4 or 2 on some symbols of Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, MEXC, Aster and Phemex

contractType.description: linear = USDT-margined (default), inverse = coin-margined. size is USD notional (contracts) for inverse; notional/funding_cost/fee_total/total_carry_cost come back denominated in the base coin.

tools.name: workflow.run_crypto_profit
tools.title: Crypto Profit
tools.description: Profit or loss on a spot crypto trade (coins bought and sold outright, no leverage, no funding) after both fees. Give exactly one of investment (total cash spent, buy fee included) or quantity (coins bought). Each fee is a fraction of that fill's trade value (0.001 = 0.1%): the buy fee is paid on top of the coins' cost, the sell fee comes out of the sale value. For a leveraged perpetual futures position see workflow.run_pnl_planning. Use when user asks "I bought BTC at $X, what is my profit if I sell at $Y?" or "what price do I need to sell at to break even after fees?". Returns: quantity, totalCost, proceeds, totalFees, profit, roiPct and priceChangePct (fractions), priceMultiple, breakevenSellPrice, annualizedReturnPct (a fraction, only when holdingDays is given and is at least 30, null otherwise: annualizing a shorter hold gives meaningless figures).

buyPrice.description: Price paid per coin, in the quote currency (e.g. 60000 for BTC in USD)

sellPrice.description: Price per coin at the sale, or the price to test, same currency

investment.description: Total cash spent on the buy, buy fee included (e.g. 1000). Give this or quantity, not both

quantity.description: Number of coins bought (e.g. 0.5). Give this or investment, not both

buyFeePct.description: Buy fee as a fraction of the trade value, 0 to 0.05 (0.001 = 0.1%). Default 0

sellFeePct.description: Sell fee as a fraction of the trade value, 0 to 0.05 (0.001 = 0.1%). Default 0

holdingDays.description: Optional: days the coins were held; 30 or more also returns the annualized return

tools.name: workflow.run_present_value
tools.title: Present Value
tools.description: Present value of a future lump sum, a level payment stream, or both: what money received later is worth today at a discount rate. annualRate is a fraction (0.05 = 5%) split into periodsPerYear equal periods the nominal way (rate per period = annualRate / periodsPerYear); years x periodsPerYear is the number of periods, which must be whole when a payment is given. Payments are level and arrive at the end of each period, or at the start with paymentTiming "begin" (annuity due). Money received is positive, money paid is negative. A bond priced at its coupon rate comes back at its face value. For a list of uneven cash flows use workflow.run_npv. Use when user asks "what is $10,000 in 5 years worth today at 6%?" or "what is a 20-year stream of $500 monthly payments worth today?". Returns: presentValue, pvOfFutureValue, pvOfPayments, discountFactor, ratePerPeriod, periods, totalPayments, effectiveAnnualRate.

annualRate.description: Annual discount rate as a fraction (0.06 = 6%); may be zero or negative, but the rate per period must stay above -100%

years.description: Length in years, 0 to 1000 (fractions allowed for a lump sum; with payments years x periodsPerYear must be a whole number)

periodsPerYear.description: Compounding and payment periods per year, 1 to 365. Default 1 (12 = monthly)

futureValue.description: Lump sum received at the end, in any currency. Default 0

paymentTiming.description: "end" (ordinary annuity, default) or "begin" (annuity due, each payment one period earlier)

tools.name: workflow.run_future_value
tools.title: Future Value
tools.description: Future value of a starting sum, regular contributions, or both, grown at a fixed rate: what savings or an investment reach after a number of years. annualRate is a fraction (0.07 = 7%) split into periodsPerYear equal periods the nominal way (rate per period = annualRate / periodsPerYear); years x periodsPerYear is the number of periods, which must be whole when a payment is given. Contributions are level and made at the end of each period, or at the start with paymentTiming "begin". A fixed assumed rate, not a forecast and not a market-return simulation (for a range of outcomes use workflow.run_monte_carlo). Use when user asks "what will $10,000 plus $500 a month be worth in 30 years at 7%?" or "how much will I have after 10 years of saving?". Returns: futureValue, fvOfPresentValue, fvOfPayments, growthFactor, ratePerPeriod, periods, totalContributions, interestEarned, effectiveAnnualRate.

annualRate.description: Annual growth rate as a fraction (0.07 = 7%); may be zero or negative, but the rate per period must stay above -100%

years.description: Length in years, 0 to 1000 (fractions allowed for a lump sum; with payments years x periodsPerYear must be a whole number)

periodsPerYear.description: Compounding and contribution periods per year, 1 to 365. Default 1 (12 = monthly)

presentValue.description: Starting amount, in any currency. Default 0

tools.name: workflow.run_npv
tools.title: Npv
tools.description: Net present value of a list of cash flows at a discount rate per period. The first flow is at time 0 and is NOT discounted (the usual textbook NPV; a spreadsheet NPV() function discounts the first value one period, so its result is this one divided by 1 + rate). Money received is positive, money paid is negative. ratePerPeriod must match the spacing of the flows (a monthly rate for monthly flows). To find the rate that makes NPV zero use workflow.run_irr. Use when user asks "is this project worth doing at a 10% cost of capital?" or "what is the NPV of these cash flows?". Returns: npv, discountedFlows, pvOfInflows, pvOfOutflows, undiscountedSum, periods.

ratePerPeriod.description: Discount rate per period as a fraction (0.1 = 10% per period), above -100%, at most 1e6

cashFlows.description: Cash flow at time 0, 1, 2, ... (e.g. [-1000, 500, 500, 500]); use 0 for an empty period

tools.name: workflow.run_irr
tools.title: Irr
tools.description: Internal rate of return: the rate per period at which the NPV of a list of cash flows is zero (first flow at time 0). The flows need at least one outflow and one inflow. One sign change in the flows (all outflows first, then all inflows) gives exactly one answer, returned as irr with unique true. With several sign changes there can be several rates or none: every rate found is listed in irrs and irr is null even when only one rate was found (reason "unverified"), with reason "multiple_roots" or "none_found" otherwise, so do not quote one rate as the return. With one sign change the search reaches about 1e13 per period; beyond that reason is "none_found". The search covers rates from -99% to +9,900% per period on a 0.2% grid of ln(1 + rate); two roots closer than that, or a root where NPV only touches zero, can be missed. Give periodsPerYear to also get the annual effective rate. Use when user asks "what is the IRR of these cash flows?" or "what return does this project earn?". Returns: irr, irrs, unique, signChanges, reason, annualEffectiveRate, periods.

cashFlows.description: Cash flow at time 0, 1, 2, ... with at least one negative and one positive value (e.g. [-1000, 300, 400, 500])

periodsPerYear.description: Optional: periods per year (12 for monthly flows), 1 to 365, to also return the annual effective rate

tools.name: workflow.run_cagr
tools.title: Cagr
tools.description: Compound annual growth rate between a beginning and an ending value over a number of years: the constant yearly rate that turns one into the other, (ending / beginning)^(1 / years) - 1. A smoothed average: it hides the path and the volatility in between, and it says nothing about future growth. Both values must be positive. Use when user asks "what is the CAGR of my portfolio?" or "what yearly growth takes $10,000 to $25,000 in 8 years?". Returns: cagr, totalReturn, growthMultiple, logGrowthRate (all fractions; logGrowthRate is the continuously compounded rate).

endingValue.description: Value at the end (positive), same currency

years.description: Years between them, above 0 and at most 1000 (fractions allowed, e.g. 2.5)

tools.name: workflow.run_apy_apr_converter
tools.title: Apy Apr Converter
tools.description: Convert an APR (nominal yearly rate) to an APY (effective yearly rate) or back, for a compounding you choose. APY = (1 + APR / m)^m - 1 for m periods a year, e^APR - 1 when continuous. The same APY is a different APR at every compounding frequency, so the frequency is required: give periodsPerYear (365 daily, 12 monthly) or continuous true, not both. Rates are fractions (0.12 = 12%). It converts rate arithmetic only: it does not include fees, token price moves or the risk that a pool rate changes. Use when user asks "what APR is an 8% APY compounded daily?" or "what is 12% APR monthly as an APY?". Returns: apr, apy, periodsPerYear, continuous, ratePerPeriod, apyMinusApr, byCompounding (the same APY as an APR at annual, semiannual, quarterly, monthly, weekly, daily and continuous compounding).

direction.description: apr_to_apy converts the given APR into an APY; apy_to_apr the reverse

rate.description: The rate you have, as a fraction per year (0.12 = 12%), up to 1000. An APY must be above -1; an APR must satisfy APR / periodsPerYear above -1

periodsPerYear.description: Compounding periods a year, 1 to 365 (12 monthly, 365 daily). Omit when continuous is true

continuous.description: True for continuous compounding; then omit periodsPerYear

tools.name: workflow.run_bond_price
tools.title: Bond Price
tools.description: Price of a plain fixed-rate bond on a coupon date, with Macaulay duration, modified duration, convexity and DV01. Price = sum of the coupons and the face value discounted at the yield per period (yield / frequency), clean price, no accrued interest, so years x frequency must be a whole number of coupon periods. The yield is the nominal yearly yield to maturity compounded frequency times a year (the bond-market convention). Durations are in years, convexity in years squared. DV01 is the price fall for one basis point of yield, a positive number, the slope at the current yield and not a repricing. It does not include credit risk, call features, taxes or the day-count of a real settlement date. Use when user asks "what is a 5-year 5% coupon bond worth at a 6% yield?" or "what is the duration and DV01 of this bond?". Returns: price, pricePctOfFace, status (premium, par, discount), pvOfCoupons, pvOfFace, couponPerPeriod, periods, yieldPerPeriod, currentYield, macaulayDuration, modifiedDuration, convexity, dv01.

faceValue.description: Face (par) value repaid at maturity, above 0 (default 1000)

couponRate.description: Annual coupon rate as a fraction of face value (0.05 = 5%), 0 to 1; 0 is a zero-coupon bond

yieldRate.description: Nominal yearly yield to maturity as a fraction (0.06 = 6%), compounded frequency times a year; yield / frequency must be above -1

years.description: Years to maturity, above 0 and at most 100; years x frequency must be a whole number (5 years semiannual is 10 coupons)

frequency.description: Coupon payments a year, 1 to 12 (default 2: semiannual; 1 annual, 4 quarterly, 12 monthly)

tools.name: workflow.run_bonding_curve
tools.title: Bonding Curve
tools.description: Pump.fun-style bonding curve calculator: exact tokens received for a buy, price impact, and graduation progress. Pure constant-product math (Uniswap V2 style) using pump.fun's official virtual-reserve constants: no live lookup needed, works for any token still on the curve (not yet graduated to a real AMM pool). Use when user asks "how many tokens do I get buying X SOL on this curve?" or "will this buy graduate the token?". Returns: tokensOut, priceImpactPct, progressPctBefore/After, willGraduate, partialFill (true if the buy exceeds remaining curve capacity).

solRaisedSoFar.description: SOL already raised on the curve so far (0 for a brand-new token)

tools.name: workflow.run_impermanent_loss
tools.title: Impermanent Loss
tools.description: Impermanent loss for a liquidity-pool position: compares providing liquidity against simply holding the same tokens, at a manually-supplied entry and current price. Two modes: full_range (standard 50/50 constant-product pool, the textbook 2*sqrt(k)/(1+k)-1 closed form) or concentrated (a Uniswap-V3-style position confined to [lowerPrice, upperPrice] - IL is always worse than full_range for the same price move when the range is tight, and the position is fully single-asset, no longer earning fees, once price exits the range). impermanentLossPct is always <= 0 and is measured relative to the quote token (dimensionless, exact regardless of what the quote token is); the optional dollar figures additionally assume the quote token's own USD price stayed roughly stable (true for a stablecoin-quoted pool). Use when user asks "how much am I losing to impermanent loss?" or "is this LP position still worth it after fees?". Returns: impermanentLossPct, lpValueMultiplier, hodlValueMultiplier, inRange, lossUsd/netResultUsd (null unless depositValueUsd given).

entryPrice.description: Base token's price in quote-token terms when liquidity was deposited

currentPrice.description: Base token's current price in quote-token terms

lowerPrice.description: Range lower bound - required for concentrated mode, must be below entryPrice

upperPrice.description: Range upper bound - required for concentrated mode, must be above entryPrice

depositValueUsd.description: Optional: USD value deposited at entry, to also report dollar-denominated lpValueUsd/hodlValueUsd/lossUsd

feesEarnedUsd.description: Optional trading fees earned so far in USD (default 0), folded into netResultUsd alongside lossUsd

tools.name: workflow.run_options_payoff
tools.title: Options Payoff
tools.description: Payoff, P&L, and breakeven price for a single-leg Deribit BTC/ETH option (long or short call/put) at a given scenario price at expiry. Deribit BTC/ETH options are coin-settled: premium, P&L, and the max profit/loss caps come back denominated in the base coin (BTC/ETH), not USD; a scenarioPnlUsd convenience field converts the coin P&L back to USD at the scenario price. Coin settlement means a long call's upside is capped (max profit = 1 − premium per unit, not unlimited) while a long put's upside is technically unbounded as price falls toward zero, the mirror image of a USD-settled option's payoff shape, not a bug. Use when user asks "what does my BTC call/put pay off at price X?" or "where's my breakeven on this option?". Returns: intrinsicPerUnitCoin, scenarioPnlCoin, scenarioPnlUsd, breakevenPrice, maxLossCoin/maxProfitCoin (null = unbounded), isProfitable.

premiumCoin.description: Premium paid/received per contract, in the base coin (matches Deribit's own quoted price, e.g. 0.02 BTC); must be < 1 for a call

quantity.description: Number of contracts (Deribit BTC/ETH options have contract_size 1.0, so this is coin-denominated size)

scenarioPrice.description: Underlying price in USD to evaluate the payoff at

tools.name: workflow.run_black_scholes
tools.title: Black-Scholes Option Price and Greeks
tools.description: Theoretical European option price and Greeks (delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho) from Black-Scholes, given manual spot/strike/days-to-expiry/volatility/risk-free-rate inputs plus an optional continuous dividend yield for stocks and ETFs (the implied-volatility and option-chain tools do not take one): no live data fetch. The live variant is workflow.run_black_scholes_live, which applies when checking a real Deribit, Binance or Bybit instrument, since that variant also reports how far the instrument's actual quoted price sits from what this formula implies. Prices are USD-denominated (the universal convention); callPriceCoin/putPriceCoin additionally divide by spot to match Deribit's own coin-settled quoting convention. Use when user asks "what should this option be worth at X% IV?" or wants raw Greeks for a hypothetical. Returns: callPriceUsd/putPriceUsd, callPriceCoin/putPriceCoin, deltaCall/deltaPut, gamma, vegaPerPct (per 1 vol point), thetaCallPerDay/thetaPutPerDay, rhoCallPerPct/rhoPutPerPct (per 1 rate point).

daysToExpiry.description: Calendar days until expiry (can be fractional)

volatilityPct.description: Annualized implied volatility in percentage points, e.g. 60 for 60%

riskFreeRatePct.description: Risk-free rate in percentage points. Default 0: standard crypto-options convention.

dividendYieldPct.description: Continuous dividend yield in percent per year (1.2 means 1.2%), for stock and ETF options. Default 0: crypto has none. Range 0 to 100.

tools.name: workflow.run_option_greeks
tools.title: Option Greeks
tools.description: First and second order Greeks of a European option from Black-Scholes-Merton, manual inputs only (no live data): everything workflow.run_black_scholes returns (price, delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho) plus the higher-order Greeks vanna, vomma (volga), charm, veta, speed, zomma and color, with an optional continuous dividend yield for stocks and ETFs. Use when the user asks how delta changes when volatility or time moves (vanna, charm), how vega changes (vomma, veta) or how gamma changes (speed, zomma, color), or for an "option greeks calculator". Units: vannaPerVolPct = change of delta per 1 volatility point; vommaPerVolPct = change of vegaPerPct per 1 volatility point; charmCallPerDay/charmPutPerDay = change of delta when one calendar day passes; vetaPerDay = change of vegaPerPct when one calendar day passes; speedPerUsd = change of gamma per 1 unit of spot; zommaPerVolPct = change of gamma per 1 volatility point; colorPerDay = change of gamma when one calendar day passes. Time Greeks are the change as time passes (the derivative with respect to time to expiry, sign flipped); one input moves, the others stay fixed. Vanna, vomma, veta, speed, zomma and color are the same for the call and the put; charm differs by the dividend term only. A calendar day is 1/365 year.

strike.description: Strike price, same units as spot

daysToExpiry.description: Calendar days until expiry (can be fractional), 0.001 to 36500

volatilityPct.description: Annualized implied volatility in percentage points, e.g. 60 for 60%, 0.01 to 1000

riskFreeRatePct.description: Risk-free rate in percentage points, 0 to 100. Default 0.

dividendYieldPct.description: Continuous dividend yield in percent per year, 0 to 100. Default 0.

tools.name: workflow.run_straddle_strangle
tools.title: Straddle and Strangle
tools.description: Payoff, P&L, and both breakeven prices for a long or short straddle/strangle (a call + a put on the same Deribit BTC/ETH underlying, both legs the same direction) at a scenario price. A straddle is callStrike === putStrike; any callStrike > putStrike makes it a strangle, same formula either way. Coin-settled like workflow.run_options_payoff: a long position's max loss is the flat total premium paid (between the strikes, both legs worthless); max profit is technically unbounded, dominated by the put leg's payoff as price falls toward zero. Use when user asks about a straddle or strangle, e.g. "what does a BTC straddle pay off if price barely moves?" or "where are my breakevens on this strangle?". Returns: combinedIntrinsicCoin, scenarioPnlCoin, scenarioPnlUsd, upperBreakevenPrice, lowerBreakevenPrice, maxLossCoin/maxProfitCoin (null = unbounded), isStraddle, isProfitable.

callStrike.description: Call leg strike, USD. Equal to putStrike for a straddle, higher for a strangle.

putStrike.description: Put leg strike, USD. Must be <= callStrike.

callPremiumCoin.description: Call leg premium per contract, in the base coin (e.g. 0.02 BTC)

putPremiumCoin.description: Put leg premium per contract, in the base coin

quantity.description: Number of straddle/strangle units (both legs sized equally)

scenarioPrice.description: Underlying price in USD to evaluate the payoff at

tools.name: workflow.run_covered_call_protective_put
tools.title: Covered Call and Protective Put
tools.description: Covered call (long the coin + short a call against it, for yield) or protective put (long the coin + long a put, for downside insurance) on a Deribit BTC/ETH position. Returns the standard annualized-yield metric (premium ÷ 1 coin, annualized by 365/daysToExpiry) up front: that number doesn't depend on any price scenario. Also returns the USD value of the combined position at a given scenario price: covered call caps upside at strike + premium×scenarioPrice (the premium's own coin-denominated value still scales with price, unlike a textbook USD-settled cap); protective put floors value at strike×(1−premium), which is the true minimum across every possible settlement price, not just an approximation. Use when user asks "what annualized yield do I get selling covered calls on my BTC?" or "how much does insuring my BTC with a put cost me?". Returns: staticYieldPct, annualizedYieldPct, valueAtScenarioUsd, breakevenPrice (covered_call only), floorValueUsd (protective_put only), vsHoldingUsd (vs. just holding the coin).

strategy.description: "covered_call" (hold the coin, sell a call against it) or "protective_put" (hold the coin, buy a put as insurance)

spotEntry.description: Price you acquired/value the underlying coin at, USD; used for the covered-call breakeven vs. cost basis

premiumCoin.description: Premium received (covered_call) or paid (protective_put) per contract, in the base coin

daysToExpiry.description: Calendar days until expiry; used to annualize the yield/cost

scenarioPrice.description: Underlying price in USD to evaluate the combined position's value at

tools.name: workflow.run_spread_payoff
tools.title: Spread Payoff
tools.description: Payoff, breakeven(s), and max profit/loss for a Deribit BTC/ETH vertical spread (2 legs, same option type, opposite direction, e.g. a bull call spread) or an iron condor/butterfly (4 legs: 2 calls + 2 puts) at a scenario price. Coin-settled, and the max profit/loss are genuinely NOT the flat, textbook USD-settled values: because each leg's own payoff is divided by the settlement price, (1) a debit vertical spread's peak payoff occurs exactly at its short strike, not "anywhere beyond it" - and its profit is a finite WINDOW that closes again at a high enough price, decaying back toward a full loss of the premium paid, and (2) an iron condor/butterfly's max loss is genuinely UNBOUNDED toward price->0 (maxLossCoin: null) if it has a put wing, unlike the "capped at wing width" USD-settled result - only the call side is actually bounded. Use when user asks about a bull/bear call/put spread, vertical spread, iron condor, or iron butterfly, e.g. "what's my max loss on this BTC call spread?" or "where do my iron condor breakevens sit?". Returns: structureType (vertical_spread/iron_condor/iron_butterfly, inferred from the legs given), netDebitCoin (negative = credit received), scenarioPayoffCoin, scenarioPnlCoin/Usd, breakevenPrices (0-3, ascending), maxLossCoin/maxProfitCoin (null = unbounded), isProfitable.

legs.description: Exactly 2 legs (same option type, opposite position - a vertical spread) or 4 legs (2 calls + 2 puts - an iron condor/butterfly). Each leg: { optionType: call|put, position: long|short, strike: number, premiumCoin: number }.

premiumCoin.description: Premium per contract, in the base coin

scenarioPrice.description: Underlying price in USD to evaluate the payoff at

tools.name: workflow.run_implied_volatility
tools.title: Implied Volatility
tools.description: Solves for the volatility that makes Black-Scholes reproduce an observed option price (Newton-Raphson with a bisection fallback for cases where vega is too flat to converge, e.g. deep ITM/OTM or very short-dated). Checks the price against its no-arbitrage bounds first and refuses to solve (converged: false + error) rather than return a garbage number when the price is impossible for the given spot/strike/rate. Use when user asks "what IV does this option price imply?" or gives a market price and wants the volatility, not the reverse. Returns: impliedVolatilityPct, iterations, method (newton-raphson/bisection), converged, identifiable, warning, priceAtSolution. identifiable is false when many volatilities reproduce the price (deep ITM, far OTM): warning then says the returned volatility is one of them. When converged is false, identifiable is false and error explains.

daysToExpiry.description: Calendar days until expiry (can be fractional)

riskFreeRatePct.description: Risk-free rate in percentage points. Default 0: standard crypto-options convention.

targetPriceUsd.description: The observed option price, USD, to solve the implied volatility from

tools.name: workflow.run_barrier_touch
tools.title: Barrier Touch
tools.description: Probability that the price touches a barrier (a target or a stop level) at ANY time within N days, under geometric Brownian motion (reflection principle with drift). This is not the probability of finishing beyond the level at expiry: at zero log-drift a touch is exactly twice as likely as a finish, and `finishBeyondProbabilityPct` is returned next to it for comparison (the end-of-window question itself is `workflow.run_window_fair_value`). Barrier above spot gives an up-touch, below spot a down-touch. Monitoring is continuous (every instant, not daily closes or candle highs, which touch less often); year is 365 days; `driftPct` is the annualized expected price drift, default 0. Output: touchProbabilityPct, finishBeyondProbabilityPct, direction, barrierDistancePct.

barrier.description: The level to touch, same units as spot. Above spot: up-touch; below spot: down-touch

daysToExpiry.description: Calendar days in the window (can be fractional, up to 3650)

volatilityPct.description: Annualized volatility in percentage points (e.g. 60 for 60%), at least 0.01

driftPct.description: Annualized expected price drift in percentage points. Default 0.

tools.name: workflow.run_american_option
tools.title: American Option
tools.description: Price of an AMERICAN put or call (exercisable on any day up to expiry) on a Cox-Ross-Rubinstein binomial tree with early exercise checked at every node, with a continuous dividend yield. Use it for stock and ETF style options; crypto options on Deribit and Binance are European (`workflow.run_black_scholes`). Output: americanPrice, delta, gamma, thetaPerDay (calendar day, read from the tree, typically 0 when exercising now is optimal), intrinsicValue, earlyExerciseNow (a tree reading: exercising now beats holding), europeanPrice (Black-Scholes, same inputs), earlyExercisePremium, europeanTreePrice and treeError (what the chosen step count costs: the same tree without early exercise minus the exact European price). More steps are closer to the exact value, not smoothly. Rates 0 to 100 percent, dividend yield is a continuous yield, not dated dividends; steps are a whole number from 50 to 2000 (default 500). Prices are USD per unit of underlying.

strike.description: Strike price, same units as spot

volatilityPct.description: Annualized volatility in percentage points (e.g. 30 for 30%), at most 300

riskFreeRatePct.description: Annual risk-free rate in percent, 0 to 100. Default 0.

dividendYieldPct.description: Continuous dividend yield in percent per year, 0 to 100. Default 0.

steps.description: Binomial tree steps, whole number from 50 to 2000. Default 500.

tools.name: workflow.run_options_position
tools.title: Options Position
tools.description: Profit and loss at expiry for a US-style equity, ETF or index option position built from 1 to 4 option legs, in US dollars with the standard contract multiplier of 100 shares (NOT Deribit and not coin-settled: for BTC/ETH options on Deribit use workflow.run_spread_payoff or workflow.run_options_payoff). Each leg: call or put, long or short, strike, premium per share as quoted, contracts. Optional `stock` adds long shares held with the options (covered call, protective put, collar). Prices are the ones you pass in; nothing is fetched. All legs share one expiry (a calendar spread is not computed). Returns: the strategy name derived from the legs (bull/bear call or put spread, iron condor, iron butterfly, straddle, strangle, covered call, protective put, collar, single leg, or a custom position), net debit or credit in dollars, maxProfitUsd and maxLossUsd (null = unlimited), every breakeven price per share, the P&L at each price in `scenarioPrices` and a short exact payoff curve. maxLossUsd is the worst P&L as a loss amount (negative if no price loses); maxProfitUsd is the best P&L (negative if every price loses).

legs.description: One to four option legs. Each leg: { optionType: call|put, position: long|short, strike: number, premium: number (USD per share), contracts: integer >= 1 (default 1) }.

strike.description: Strike price, USD per share, above 0

premium.description: Premium per share as quoted, USD, 0 or more. A contract covers 100 shares, so a 4.50 premium costs 450 dollars per contract.

contracts.description: Number of contracts, a whole number from 1. Default 1.

stock.description: Optional long shares held together with the options: { quantity: whole shares, costPerShare: USD }. 100 shares cover one short call.

scenarioPrices.description: Expiry prices (USD per share, 0 or more) to report the position P&L at. Optional.

tools.name: workflow.run_strategy_picker
tools.title: Strategy Picker
tools.description: Ranks option strategies for a price forecast and a volatility view. You give the spot price, the price you expect at expiry, days to expiry and the market implied volatility; optionally your own volatility forecast (default: the market's, so the view is on price only). Every strategy is built from strikes on a grid around spot, each leg priced with Black-Scholes at the one implied volatility (no skew, no dividends), and the best-fitting version of each family is kept: long call, long put, short put (cash-secured), covered call, protective put, long straddle, long strangle, bull call spread, bear call spread, bull put spread, bear put spread, long call butterfly, short iron condor, short iron butterfly; with allowUnlimitedLoss also naked short call, short straddle and short strangle. The view is a lognormal distribution whose mean is targetPrice and whose volatility is forecastVolPct. Per 1 unit of the underlying (multiply by contract size), each strategy returns its legs, net premium, max profit and max loss (null = unlimited), breakevens, expected profit under the view, probability of profit, and return on risk (expected profit / max loss). rankBy: expectedPnl (default), returnOnRisk (favours far out-of-the-money options) or probabilityOfProfit. Not a recommendation: the result is only as good as the forecast, and premiums are not discounted. Prices are computed, nothing is fetched; for equity options with quoted premiums use workflow.run_options_position.

spot.description: Current price of the underlying, from 0.000000001 to 1000000000

targetPrice.description: Price you expect at expiry (the mean of your view), from 0.000000001 to 1000000000

daysToExpiry.description: Days to expiry, above 0 and at most 3650

impliedVolPct.description: Market implied volatility in percent per year (e.g. 30), used to price every option, at most 1000

forecastVolPct.description: Your own volatility forecast in percent per year. Default: impliedVolPct (no volatility view).

riskFreeRatePct.description: Annual risk-free rate in percent, 0 to 100. Default 0.

strikeStep.description: Strike spacing. Default: a round step that gives about 16 strikes across the range, plus one past each end. The grid must hold 3 to 60 strikes.

allowUnlimitedLoss.description: Include naked short call, short straddle and short strangle. Default false.

tools.name: workflow.run_window_fair_value
tools.title: Window Fair Value
tools.description: Theoretical fair value for a time-windowed crypto up/down contract (the shape ADI Predictstreet and Kalshi-style daily crypto markets use: pays out based on whether the settlement price finishes at/above or below a reference price pinned at window open, by a fixed close time): a cash-or-nothing digital option, priced with the standard N(d2) formula. It gives the probability at the close time only, not the probability of touching a level at any point before it (first passage). Time convention: a year is 365 days. Use this when there's no live market price to read (e.g. a venue's contract has real terms but zero trading volume) instead of a live-market odds tool. Volatility is a required manual input; there is no live implied-vol market on these contracts to pull it from. Use when user asks "what does the N(d2) model give for this up/down contract?" or "what's the model probability BTC finishes above $X in N minutes?". Returns: d1, d2, probAbovePct, probBelowPct, fairPriceAboveCents, fairPriceBelowCents (cents convention, directly comparable to how these venues quote a contract).

currentPrice.description: Current spot price of the coin, in USD.

referencePrice.description: The reference/pinned price the contract resolves against (the window's open price, or a stated strike).

minutesToClose.description: Minutes remaining until the window closes/settles.

volatilityPct.description: Annualized volatility, in percentage points (e.g. 50 for 50%). Required; no live source for this on these contracts.

riskFreeRatePct.description: Risk-free rate in percentage points. Default 0: negligible for these short windows.

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_pip_value
tools.title: Forex Pip Value
tools.description: Value of 1 pip for a given forex pair and position size, in that pair's own quote currency (e.g. EUR/USD's pip value comes back in USD, USD/JPY's in JPY): no live FX rate needed, since a pair's pip value is naturally denominated in its own quote currency. Pip size is 0.0001 for non-JPY pairs, 0.01 for JPY-quoted pairs, a universal market convention verified against real broker documentation, not broker-specific. The live variant is workflow.run_forex_pip_value_live, which applies when the account currency differs from the pair's quote currency. Precious-metal pairs (XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD) are refused with an error, because their pip and lot size differ by broker. Use when user asks "what's 1 pip worth on X lots of EUR/USD?". Returns: pipSize, pipValueQuote, base, quote.

pair.description: Currency pair in BASE/QUOTE format, e.g. "EUR/USD"

units.description: Position size in base-currency units (1 standard lot = 100,000, mini = 10,000, micro = 1,000, nano = 100)

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_margin_level
tools.title: Forex Margin Level
tools.description: Free margin and margin level % from account equity and used margin: equity/usedMargin*100, the same stop-out proximity metric every forex platform shows. Returns null (not Infinity) when usedMargin is 0, meaning no open position. Use when user asks "how close am I to a margin call?" or "what's my free margin?". Returns: freeMargin, marginLevelPct.

usedMargin.description: Margin currently locked by open positions. 0 if none.

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_breakeven
tools.title: Forex Breakeven
tools.description: Breakeven price for a forex position accounting for spread and round-trip commission, in pips and in price. Commission is quoted per standard lot (100,000 units) and expressed in the pair's own quote currency; because both commission and pip value scale with lot size, the commission-in-pips figure is independent of position size by construction. Precious-metal pairs (XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD) are refused with an error, because their pip and lot size differ by broker. Use when user asks "where's my true breakeven after spread and commission?". Returns: pipSize, commissionPips, totalCostPips, breakevenPrice.

pair.description: Currency pair in BASE/QUOTE format, e.g. "EUR/USD"

entryPrice.description: Entry price in the pair's own quote terms, e.g. 1.0850 for EUR/USD

commissionPerLotRoundTrip.description: Round-trip commission per standard lot, in the pair's own quote currency. Default 0 (pure-spread broker model).

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_pnl
tools.title: Forex PnL
tools.description: Profit or loss for a closed or hypothetical forex trade, in pips and in the pair's own quote currency, long or short. Precious-metal pairs (XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD) are refused with an error, because their pip and lot size differ by broker. Use when user asks "what did I make/lose on this trade?" or "what would X pips be worth on Y lots?". Returns: pips (signed, positive favors the position taken), pnlQuote.

pair.description: Currency pair in BASE/QUOTE format, e.g. "EUR/USD"

entryPrice.description: Entry price in the pair's own quote terms, e.g. 1.0850 for EUR/USD

exitPrice.description: Exit price, same quote convention as the entry price

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_risk_reward
tools.title: Forex Risk Reward
tools.description: Risk and reward distance in pips from entry/stop/target, and the resulting ratio (reward/risk): a raw number, not a verdict. ratio is null when the stop sits exactly at entry (no risk distance), and also when validSetup is false (stop/target on the wrong side of entry for the given side, e.g. a long with its stop above entry) - check validSetup before trusting the ratio. Precious-metal pairs (XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD) are refused with an error, because their pip and lot size differ by broker. Use when user asks "what's my risk/reward on this setup?". Returns: riskPips, rewardPips, validSetup, ratio.

pair.description: Currency pair in BASE/QUOTE format, e.g. "EUR/USD"

entryPrice.description: Entry price in the pair's own quote terms, e.g. 1.0850 for EUR/USD

stopPrice.description: Stop-loss price, same quote convention as the entry price

targetPrice.description: Take-profit price, same quote convention as the entry price

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_scenario
tools.title: Forex Scenario
tools.description: PnL across a range of hypothetical price moves (in pips, signed by actual price direction, not pre-adjusted for side), for a single forex position size, long or short. Precious-metal pairs (XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD) are refused with an error, because their pip and lot size differ by broker. Use when user asks "what if price moves X pips in either direction?". Returns: scenarios[] (deltaPips, exitPrice, pnlQuote).

pair.description: Currency pair in BASE/QUOTE format, e.g. "EUR/USD"

entryPrice.description: Entry price in the pair's own quote terms, e.g. 1.0850 for EUR/USD

deltasPips.description: Hypothetical price moves in pips, e.g. [-50, 0, 50]

tools.name: workflow.run_fibonacci_levels
tools.title: Fibonacci Levels
tools.description: Fibonacci retracement and extension price levels from a swing high and low, for any asset (forex, stocks, crypto): retracement 0, 23.6, 38.2, 50, 61.8, 78.6 and 100 percent and extension 127.2, 161.8, 200 and 261.8 percent, as prices. direction "up" measures a rise from the low to the high, "down" a fall from the high to the low; 0 percent is the end of the swing and 100 percent its start. A level at or below zero (an extension of a steep fall) comes back as price null. The ratios are a charting convention, not a forecast. Pure price arithmetic, no pair or market data.

high.description: Swing high price (positive, above the low, at most 1e300)

low.description: Swing low price (positive, below the high)

direction.description: "up": the swing rose from the low to the high; "down": it fell from the high to the low

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_average_entry
tools.title: Forex Average Entry
tools.description: Size-weighted average entry price across multiple forex fills: plain arithmetic mean, since forex has no coin-margined analog requiring the harmonic mean the crypto average_entry tool uses for inverse contracts. Use when user asks "what's my average entry after these fills?". Returns: totalUnits, totalCost, avgEntry.

pair.description: Currency pair in BASE/QUOTE format, e.g. "EUR/USD"

fills.description: Fills to average, each with a price and a size in base-currency units

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_margin_required
tools.title: Forex Margin Required
tools.description: Notional and margin required for a forex position, in the pair's own quote currency: no live FX rate needed. Never built for Phase 1 of this domain since a margin figure has no natural currency-neutral form the way pip value does. The live variant is workflow.run_forex_margin_required_live, which applies when the account currency differs from the pair's quote currency. Use when user asks "how much margin do I need for X lots of EUR/USD at 50:1?". Returns: notionalQuote, marginQuote, base, quote.

pair.description: Currency pair in BASE/QUOTE format, e.g. "EUR/USD"

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_currency_converter
tools.title: Forex Currency Converter
tools.description: Converts an amount between currencies using a manually supplied rate: no live data fetch. The live variant is workflow.run_forex_currency_converter_live, which has the rate fetched automatically. Use when user already knows the exact rate they want applied. Returns: converted.

rate.description: Exchange rate to apply (1 unit of source currency = rate units of target currency)

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_swap_cost
tools.title: Forex Swap Cost
tools.description: Total swap/rollover cost (or credit) for holding a forex position overnight, in the pair's own quote currency: no live FX rate needed. Swap rates are broker-set with no free live feed available, so swapPerLotPerNight is always a manual input (quoted per standard lot, matching how commission is quoted in workflow.run_forex_breakeven), not fetched. Negative = cost (you pay), positive = credit (you receive). The live variant is workflow.run_forex_swap_cost_live, which applies when the account currency differs from the pair's quote currency. Precious-metal pairs (XAU, XAG, XPT, XPD) are refused with an error, because their pip and lot size differ by broker. Use when user asks "how much will holding this position overnight cost me?". Returns: lots, totalSwapQuote, base, quote.

pair.description: Currency pair in BASE/QUOTE format, e.g. "EUR/USD"

swapPerLotPerNight.description: Swap rate per standard lot (100,000 units) per night, in the pair's quote currency. Negative = cost, positive = credit. Broker-set: get this from the user's broker platform, there is no live source for it.

nights.description: Number of nights the position is held

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_correlation
tools.title: Forex Correlation
tools.description: Correlation coefficient and minimum-variance hedge ratio between two price series of matching length, computed on daily % returns (not raw price levels, which would give spuriously high correlation between two unrelated but both-trending series). hedgeRatio follows Hull's standard futures-hedging formula: cov(returns1,returns2)/var(returns2), "how many units of series 2 per unit of series 1 minimizes the combined position's variance." No live data fetch: supply the two price series directly. The live variant is workflow.run_forex_correlation_live, which has both series fetched automatically for two named pairs. Use when user already has two price series and wants their statistical relationship. Returns: n, correlation (-1 to 1), hedgeRatio.

rates1.description: First price series, chronological order, one price per date

rates2.description: Second price series, chronological order, same length and same dates as rates1

tools.name: workflow.run_var_cvar
tools.title: VaR and CVaR
tools.description: Parametric Value at Risk (VaR) and Conditional VaR / Expected Shortfall (CVaR), the variance-covariance method (assumes normally distributed returns), plus Modified VaR (Cornish-Fisher skew/kurtosis correction, Boudt/Peterson/Croux) when a return series is supplied. Supply either a return series or a mean/stdev pair directly, at a confidence level. Output is at the same periodicity as the input (no automatic annualization) - a daily return series gives a daily VaR/CVaR. Use when user asks "what's my VaR at 95%/99%?", "what's my expected shortfall on this position?", or "does my Sharpe/VaR estimate need a fat-tails correction?". Returns: var, cvar (both positive loss magnitudes; cvar >= var always), z, mean, stdev, skewness, excess_kurtosis (both null unless 3+ returns were supplied), var_modified (skew/kurtosis-adjusted VaR; null when skewness is, OR when this series' skew/kurtosis are too extreme for the Cornish-Fisher expansion to be a valid quantile - skewness/excess_kurtosis are still returned in that case).

returns.description: Return series (e.g. daily % returns as decimals). Provide this OR mean+stdev, not both.

mean.description: Mean return, if not supplying returns[] directly

stdev.description: Standard deviation of returns, if not supplying returns[] directly

tools.name: workflow.run_sharpe_stats
tools.title: Sharpe Ratio Statistics
tools.description: Sharpe ratio with the Lo (2002) serial-correlation-aware annualization correction, computed in its lag-1 form rather than the full multi-lag sum (the naive sqrt(periods_per_year) scaling overstates or understates the true annualized Sharpe when returns are autocorrelated), plus the Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio (Bailey & Lopez de Prado): the probability the true Sharpe exceeds a benchmark, adjusted for the sample's skewness/kurtosis and length, not just its point estimate. Use when user asks "what's my real annualized Sharpe, not the naive one?" or "how confident can I be this Sharpe ratio is actually good?". Returns: sharpe_period, sharpe_annualized_naive, sharpe_annualized_lo, autocorrelation_lag1, psr, skewness, kurtosis.

returns.description: Return series, one value per period

periods_per_year.description: Periods per year for annualization (default 365, crypto convention - trades every day). Any number from 1 to 100 million, e.g. 365.25.

benchmark_sharpe.description: Benchmark Sharpe ratio for the PSR test, same periodicity as returns (default 0)

tools.name: workflow.run_hurst_exponent
tools.title: Hurst Exponent
tools.description: Hurst exponent via rescaled-range (R/S) analysis: is this return/price series trending/persistent (H>0.5, a move tends to be followed by a move in the same direction), mean-reverting/anti-persistent (H<0.5), or consistent with a random walk (H~0.5)? Use when user asks "is this asset trending or mean-reverting?" or "does this series show long-range dependence?". Takes a return series, not raw price levels. Returns: hurst, interpretation (trending/mean_reverting/random_walk), window_sizes, rs_values.

tools.name: workflow.run_cointegration
tools.title: Cointegration Test
tools.description: Engle-Granger two-step cointegration test for a pair of price series: do they share a long-run equilibrium relationship (their spread is stationary/mean-reverting)? The standard pairs-trading signal test. Returns the cointegrating regression's hedge ratio (beta) and an ADF t-statistic on the residuals, compared against 1%/5%/10% critical values. Use when user asks "are these two assets cointegrated?" or "is this a valid pairs trade?". Returns: alpha, beta (hedge ratio), t_stat, critical_values, cointegrated (booleans at each significance level).

y.description: First price series (the dependent variable in the cointegrating regression)

x.description: Second price series, same length and dates as y

tools.name: workflow.run_portfolio_tearsheet
tools.title: Portfolio Tearsheet
tools.description: Core risk/return tearsheet from a single return series: annualized return (compounded, not linear) and volatility, Sharpe (plain + Lo 2002-corrected + Pezier-White skew/kurtosis-adjusted), Sortino, max drawdown, Calmar ratio, the drawdown-ratio cluster (Ulcer Index/Martin ratio, Pain Index/Pain ratio, Burke ratio + modified), Omega-Sharpe ratio, Upside Potential Ratio, skewness, kurtosis, Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio, win rate, best/worst single-period return. Use when user asks for a full risk summary/report on a strategy or portfolio's returns, not just one metric. Returns all of the above in one call. Returns are decimals (0.02 is 2%), at least 3 periods; the call returns an error when the series never draws down (Calmar undefined) or no period falls below mar (Sortino undefined).

returns.description: Return series, one value per period

periods_per_year.description: Periods per year for annualization (default 365). Any number from 1 to 100 million, e.g. 365.25.

mar.description: Minimum acceptable return for the Sortino ratio, same periodicity as returns (default 0)

benchmark_sharpe.description: Benchmark Sharpe ratio for the PSR figure, same periodicity as returns (default 0)

tools.name: workflow.run_garch
tools.title: GARCH Volatility
tools.description: GARCH(1,1) volatility model, fit by maximum likelihood on a return series: estimates omega/alpha/beta (the variance-persistence parameters) and forecasts next-period volatility. Use when user asks "what's my GARCH volatility forecast?" or "how persistent is volatility in this return series?". This is a backward-looking statistical fit, not a market prediction guarantee. Returns: mu, omega, alpha, beta, persistence (alpha+beta), unconditional_vol, forecast_vol, loglikelihood.

returns.description: Return series, one value per period, at least 50 values (GARCH needs real sample depth to identify persistence)

tools.name: workflow.run_risk_parity
tools.title: Risk Parity Weights
tools.description: Risk-parity (equal or custom risk contribution) portfolio weights for N assets: given a covariance matrix (or N return series to compute one from), finds long-only weights where each asset contributes its target share of total portfolio risk. Use when user asks "what weights give each asset equal risk contribution?" or "how do I risk-parity-weight this portfolio?". A portfolio-construction calculation, not a buy/sell recommendation. Returns: weights, risk_contributions (should match risk_budgets exactly at convergence), portfolio_volatility.

returns.description: One return series per asset (2+ assets, all series the same length). Provide this OR covariance, not both.

covariance.description: Direct NxN covariance matrix, if not supplying returns[][] directly.

risk_budgets.description: Target risk share per asset, one per asset (need not sum to 1, normalized internally). Default: equal (1/N each).

tools.name: workflow.run_dsr
tools.title: Deflated Sharpe Ratio
tools.description: Deflated Sharpe Ratio (Bailey & Lopez de Prado): given how many strategy variants you tried (and how correlated they are), what Sharpe ratio would the *best of N* clear by luck alone, and does your actual strategy still clear that higher bar? Use when user asks "is my backtested Sharpe ratio real, or did I get lucky trying many variants?" or "how many independent trials does this really represent?". Provide either trial_sharpes[] (the N trials' own observed Sharpe ratios, most rigorous) or n_trials (+ optional avg_correlation to correct for correlated trials via Kish's design effect). Two limits to know. n_trials assumes the paper's illustrative case (trial Sharpes with mean 0 and variance 1, in per-period units), which is a very high bar for a low-frequency series: the threshold is about 1.6 at N=10, 2.5 at N=100 and 3.3 at N=1000, while a daily series has a per-period Sharpe of order 0.05, so dsr comes out effectively 0; use trial_sharpes there. trial_sharpes centers the threshold on the trials' own mean Sharpe plus their dispersion times the expected-maximum factor; this answers "does my strategy beat the best of N trials drawn from the spread I observed", not the zero-skill-null variant; pass null_mean true for that variant (mean fixed at 0, spread still taken from the trials); the two thresholds differ by exactly the trials' mean Sharpe. Returns: expected_max_sharpe (the luck-alone threshold), dsr (probability your strategy's true Sharpe exceeds it, 0-1), n_trials_effective.

returns.description: The candidate strategy's own return series

trial_sharpes.description: Observed Sharpe ratios of all N trials tried, if tracked. Takes priority over n_trials if both are given.

n_trials.description: Number of strategy variants tried, if trial_sharpes were not tracked individually. Assumes trial Sharpes with mean 0 and variance 1 (per-period units): too strict for daily series, prefer trial_sharpes there.

avg_correlation.description: Average pairwise correlation between trials, 0-1 (default 0 = independent). Only used with n_trials; lowers the effective trial count via Kish's design effect.

null_mean.description: Only used with trial_sharpes. true = centre the luck threshold on 0 (zero-skill null) instead of on the trials' own mean Sharpe; the spread still comes from the trials. Default false.

tools.name: workflow.run_kelly_frontier
tools.title: Kelly Growth-Security Frontier
tools.description: Kelly growth-security frontier (MacLean, Ziemba & Blazenko 1992): for a strategy compounding at a fraction lambda of full Kelly, the probability wealth ever falls to a fraction alpha of its starting value is P = alpha^(2/lambda-1). Provide either lambda_fraction (to compute that probability) or max_probability (to solve for the largest lambda that keeps the ruin probability at or below it). Use when user asks "if I bet half-Kelly, what's my chance of ever losing half my bankroll?" or "what fraction of Kelly keeps my chance of a 50% drawdown under 5%?". Valid lambda range is (0, 2]; beyond 2 the probability is certain (1), not the raw formula value. Returns: probability, lambda_fraction (echoed or solved).

alpha.description: Fraction of starting capital, 0-1 exclusive (e.g. 0.5 = "ever falls to half my starting bankroll")

lambda_fraction.description: Fraction of full Kelly being bet (1 = full Kelly, 0.5 = half Kelly). Provide this OR max_probability, not both.

max_probability.description: Target ceiling on the ruin probability, 0-1 exclusive. Provide this to solve for the safe lambda_fraction instead of supplying it directly.

tools.name: workflow.run_unsmoothing
tools.title: Return Unsmoothing
tools.description: Return "unsmoothing" for infrequently-marked/illiquid or appraisal-based series: Getmansky-Lo-Makarov (2004) MA(2) smoothing index plus Blundell-Ward (1987) AR(1) volatility inflation, two complementary models answering "this return series looks smoother than it really is; what's the true volatility?". Use when user asks "how much is appraisal smoothing understating my real volatility?" or "what's my de-smoothed Sharpe ratio?". Returns: glm_theta (MA(2) weights), glm_smoothing_index (xi, 1=no smoothing, down to 1/3 for max MA(2) smoothing), glm_true_volatility_multiplier, glm_converged (false if the fit may be unreliable - treat that result with caution), bw_alpha (AR(1) coefficient = lag-1 autocorrelation, can be negative), bw_smoothing_detected (false when alpha<=0: no evidence of smoothing, bw_volatility_multiplier is then pinned to 1 with no correction applied rather than a misleading below-1 value), bw_volatility_multiplier, and each model's own true_stdev estimate.

returns.description: The observed (possibly smoothed) return series, at least 20 values
