tools.name: workflow.run_evt_tail_risk
tools.title: EVT Tail Risk
tools.description: Extreme Value Theory tail risk (Peaks-Over-Threshold): fits a Generalized Pareto Distribution to the losses beyond a high threshold via Grimshaw's (1993) profile-likelihood MLE, then extrapolates VaR/Expected Shortfall at the requested confidence, without assuming a normal distribution. Use when user asks "what's my tail VaR without assuming normality?" or "how fat is my loss tail, really?". Complements workflow.run_var_cvar (parametric, normal-distribution VaR/CVaR) for exactly the fat-tailed-return case that assumption understates. threshold_percentile (default 90) sets which percentile of the loss distribution (losses = -returns) becomes the threshold u; confidence must be deep enough into the fitted tail (1-confidence < the threshold's own exceedance rate) or the call throws. Returns: threshold, n_exceedances, exceedance_rate, xi (GPD shape: 0=exponential tail, >0=heavy/fat tail, <0=bounded tail; values <= -1 are excluded from the fit domain as a known non-regular/unbounded-likelihood case, Smith 1985), beta (GPD scale), xi_asymptotically_normal (false when xi<=-0.5: the fit is still valid but the usual MLE confidence-interval theory doesn't apply, per that same Smith 1985 result), var, es (null when xi>=1, where Expected Shortfall is mathematically undefined).

returns.description: Return series, one value per period, at least 100 values (POT needs real sample depth in the tail)

threshold_percentile.description: Percentile (0-100 exclusive) of the loss distribution used as the POT threshold u. Default 90.

confidence.description: VaR/ES confidence level, 0-1 exclusive. Default 0.99. Must satisfy 1-confidence < the threshold's own exceedance rate.

tools.name: workflow.run_monte_carlo
tools.title: Monte Carlo Simulation
tools.description: Monte Carlo simulation of a portfolio: geometric Brownian motion with a contribution (or withdrawal) at the end of every step, up to 10,000 paths (paths x steps at most 5 million), deterministic for a given seed. Returns the spread of final values (percentiles 5 to 95, mean with its standard error and the exact expected value, probability of ending below the net amount invested, probability of ending a step at or below a ruin level) and a fan of 5th, 50th and 95th percentile bands over time, instead of one number. A value that would go below zero is floored at zero. Constant return and volatility, no fees or taxes: a model of spread, not a forecast. Use when user asks "what range of outcomes can my portfolio end in", "how likely is it that I run out of money withdrawing X a month" or "simulate my savings plan".

initialValue.description: Starting value, 0 to 1e12. 0 is allowed only with a positive contribution.

contributionPerStep.description: Added at the END of every step; negative is a withdrawal. Default 0.

annualReturnPct.description: Expected growth mu in percentage points per year, -100 to 500.

volatilityPct.description: Annual volatility sigma in percentage points, 0 to 500.

years.description: Horizon in years, above 0 and at most 50. years x stepsPerYear must be a whole number.

stepsPerYear.description: Steps (and contributions) per year, 1 to 365. Default 12.

paths.description: Simulated paths, 100 to 10000 (paths x steps at most 5 million). Default 2000.

seed.description: Random seed, 0 to 4294967295; the same input and seed give the same result. Default 1.

ruinBelow.description: A path counts as ruined once it ends a step at or below this value. Default 0.

tools.name: workflow.run_orderbook_impact
tools.title: Orderbook Impact
tools.description: Order-book "walk the book" impact/capacity: given order-book levels (price, size in base-asset units) and EITHER a target notional or an impact budget in bps, computes VWAP and price impact for that size, or (via bisection) the largest notional that stays inside the impact budget. Use when user asks "what's my price impact if I trade $X" or "how much can I trade before impact exceeds Y bps". side="buy" walks the asks, side="sell" walks the bids; impact is measured from the book's own mid ((best_bid+best_ask)/2) and is always a positive "cost in bps" number regardless of side. Returns: mid_price, spread_bps, vwap, impact_bps - both null when EITHER the loaded book doesn't cover the requested notional (book_sufficient=false flags this specific case) OR the notional involved is ~0 (book_sufficient stays true then; happens for a near-zero notional_usd, or in capacity mode when even an infinitesimal trade already exceeds impact_budget_bps, in which case max_notional itself resolves to 0) - and in capacity mode, max_notional plus capacity_is_lower_bound (true if the ENTIRE supplied book was consumed within budget, meaning true market capacity may exceed what was supplied - this tool only sees the levels given to it).

bids.description: Bid levels as [price, size_base] pairs, any order

asks.description: Ask levels as [price, size_base] pairs, any order

side.description: "buy" walks the asks, "sell" walks the bids

notional_usd.description: Target notional to walk the book for. Provide this OR impact_budget_bps, not both.

impact_budget_bps.description: Max acceptable impact in bps; solves for the largest notional within it. Provide this OR notional_usd, not both.

tools.name: workflow.run_open_analysis
tools.title: Market Profile: Open Analysis
tools.description: Market Profile open analysis: where and how price opened vs the prior session value area. Use for "how did BTC open today?" / "what does the open imply for the session?". Returns: open_location, open_type (OD/OTD/ORR/OAIR) with description/implication, confidence, key_levels (VAH/VAL/VPOC/IB), tails (session-high/low rejection tails and single prints), scenario_framing (bullish/bearish/neutral), invalidation level. Candles come from the venue when candles[] is omitted (past sessions are cached, so repeats are fast); supplying candles[] makes the run network-free and reproducible. session_date must be a completed UTC session, before today; a session with no candles returns an error.

venue.description: Exchange to fetch candles from when candles[] not supplied

session_date.description: Session date YYYY-MM-DD (UTC); must be before today (a completed session)

candles.description: Optional OHLCV for the session; omit to fetch from venue (reproducible + 0 COGS when supplied)

prev_candles.description: Optional OHLCV for the previous session

tools.title: Market Profile: Session Structure
tools.description: Market Profile day-type classifier: trend / balance / neutral_trend / normal / normal_var, from TPO, initial balance, range extension and value migration. Use for "is this a trend day or a balance day?". Returns: structure (the day-type label), description, bias, key_signals, key_levels (VAH/VAL/VPOC/IB/session high-low), tails (session-high/low rejection tails and single prints), scenario_framing, invalidation level. Candles come from the venue when candles[] is omitted (past sessions are cached, so repeats are fast); supplying candles[] makes the run network-free and reproducible. session_date must be a completed UTC session, before today; a session with no candles returns an error.

tools.name: workflow.run_token_risk_check
tools.title: Token Risk Check
tools.description: Token rug-pull MECHANISM check for a Solana token (mint address): can the deployer still mint supply, freeze wallets, pull liquidity, swap metadata, or has RugCheck flagged a known scam pattern (e.g. copycat token)? Fetches live facts from RugCheck (GoPlus as fallback) and returns a transparently-weighted composite score. Deliberately does NOT score holder concentration or "whale dump" impact: those are properties of any liquid market (a legit protocol's top holders are routinely treasury/vesting/exchange wallets), not rug signals; they are returned separately as informational market_context. Use when user asks "is this token a rug pull?" or "is [token] safe to buy?". This is a sourced, timestamped read of public facts, not a safety guarantee. Returns: score (0-100), verdict (clean/caution/high_risk/red_flags), verdict_summary, components breakdown, facts, market_context, sources.

tools.name: workflow.run_swap_price_impact
tools.title: Swap Price Impact
tools.description: Live price-impact quote for a Solana token swap: routed through Jupiter (the same aggregator real swaps use) across every pool it knows about, not a single-pool estimate. Works in both directions: side "sell" (default) sells a token into USDC or SOL, side "buy" spends USDC or SOL to buy the token. Use when user asks "how much slippage will I eat swapping X tokens?", "what will I actually get if I sell N tokens?" or "what do I get buying this token with 500 SOL?". Returns: side, outputAmount (quote asset when selling, tokens when buying), priceImpactPct, effectivePrice (quote asset per token in both directions), marketPriceUsd, liquidityUsd, routable (false + error if the size can't be routed at all).

mint.description: Solana mint address of the token being sold or bought (base58)

amount.description: Amount to swap, in human units (not raw base units): tokens when side is sell, units of outputAsset to spend when side is buy

outputAsset.description: The quote asset: received when selling, paid with when buying. Default USDC.

side.description: sell: sell the token for outputAsset (default). buy: spend outputAsset to buy the token.

tools.name: workflow.run_market_cap_comparison

tools.description: Compares two tokens' live market caps (Solana or any of 5 EVM chains; the two tokens can be on different chains) and projects what an investment would be worth if the first token's market cap matched the second's. Narrative-agnostic ("if X reaches Y's market cap"): works for any token pair, not tied to one hype cycle or one chain. A snapshot ratio, not a forecast: assumes fixed supply on both sides. Use when user asks "what if this token reaches [other token]'s market cap?". Returns: multiplier, projectedValueUsd, projectedPriceUsd, profitUsd, comparable (false + error if either market cap can't be resolved).

Returns the same fields as workflow.run_impermanent_loss, plus currentPrice, baseSymbol, quoteSymbol, routable (false + error if either token's price can't be resolved).

tools.name: workflow.run_wallet_flag_check
tools.title: Wallet Flag Check
tools.description: Checks a wallet address (Solana or any of 5 EVM chains) against independent flag databases: GoPlus (malicious-address categories, all chains), Webacy (address analysis + sanctions check, all chains), and ScamSniffer (public phishing/drainer blacklist, EVM chains only), and returns each source's own facts separately, never merged into one invented score. Use when user asks "is this wallet address flagged?" or "is it safe to send to this address?". A clean result means "nothing found in these databases," not a certified-safe verdict. Returns: goplus (flags[], categoriesChecked), webacyGeneral (overallRisk, dprk/hack/ofacSanctioned, exchangeLabel), webacySanctions (status), scamSniffer (flagged; not applicable on Solana). Each source has an `available` flag: false + error if that source failed independently.

chain.description: Chain of the wallet address. Default solana.

walletAddress.description: Wallet address (base58 for Solana, 0x... for EVM chains)

tools.name: workflow.run_odds_converter
tools.title: Odds Converter
tools.description: Converts one probability into decimal odds, American odds, and breakeven win rate: either from a manually supplied probability, or from one market read live from Kalshi, Polymarket, ADI Predictstreet, Limitless, or Myriad (five independent crypto-price prediction market venues, all public keyless market data). One market on one venue per call; it does not compare prices across venues (to compare the same bet on two or more venues, see workflow.run_spread_reader). When a Kalshi, Polymarket, Limitless, or Myriad source is supplied, also returns the vig (the exchange's built-in edge), computed from the market's own YES+NO prices, not estimated; ADI Predictstreet's crypto contracts currently have no live trading volume on any venue, so this returns available:false with an explanation rather than a fake price (use workflow.run_window_fair_value for a theoretical price on those instead). Use when user asks "what odds does a 35% probability work out to?" or "what's the vig on this Kalshi/Polymarket/Limitless/Myriad market?". Provide exactly one of probability/kalshiTicker/polymarketSlug/adiSymbol/limitlessSlug/myriadSlug. Returns: probability, decimalOdds, americanOdds, breakevenWinRatePct, vigPct (null unless a live two-sided source was used), source (manual/kalshi/polymarket/adi/limitless/myriad), identifier, label. If available is false, do not use any result field (computed figures and any verdict are null or empty), so read available first.

probability.description: Probability as a decimal 0-1 (e.g. 0.35). Use this OR one of the live sources below, not both.

kalshiTicker.description: A Kalshi market ticker (e.g. KXBTCY-27JAN0100-T149999.99) to fetch a live price from. One market only; for the same bet on several venues use workflow.run_spread_reader.

polymarketSlug.description: A Polymarket market slug, from the market URL (e.g. will-bitcoin-reach-100k-in-september-2026), to fetch a live price from. One market only; for the same bet on several venues use workflow.run_spread_reader.

adiSymbol.description: An ADI Predictstreet market symbol (e.g. BTC1D-20260920T0000). Currently always returns available:false; these contracts have no live trading volume yet.

limitlessSlug.description: A Limitless Exchange market slug, from the market URL (e.g. btc-up-or-down-5-min-1790249100), to fetch a live price from. On-chain (Base), mostly short-duration (5min/15min/daily) crypto up/down contracts.

myriadSlug.description: A Myriad Markets market slug, from the market URL (e.g. eth-at-three-digits-when-bitcoin-goes-below-50k), to fetch a live price from. On-chain (Abstract L2); not every market has a Yes/No outcome, some are multi-outcome ladders.

tools.name: workflow.run_spread_reader
tools.title: Spread Reader
tools.description: Reads the same real-world bet's live price from 2-5 prediction-market venues at once (Kalshi, Polymarket, ADI Predictstreet, Limitless, Myriad) in a single call and reports the spread between the cheapest and most expensive. Takes every venue's identifier together in quotes[], for example one Kalshi ticker and one Polymarket slug for the same bet, and returns the venue with the lowest yes midpoint price, before fees and depth. The caller supplies each venue's own identifier for what they've confirmed is the same underlying bet; this tool never auto-matches events across venues, only reads and compares prices for identifiers you provide. For the odds, breakeven win rate or vig of a single market, see workflow.run_odds_converter. Use when user asks "is this bet priced differently on Kalshi vs Polymarket?" or "which venue quotes the lowest yes price on this?". Returns: quotes[] (venue, identifier, label, probabilityPct, available, error), availableCount, cheapestVenue, mostExpensiveVenue, spreadPct (percentage points, null if fewer than 2 quotes resolved).

venue.description: Prediction-market venue this quote comes from

identifier.description: Kalshi ticker, Polymarket slug, ADI Predictstreet symbol, Limitless slug, or Myriad slug, matching the venue field.

quotes.description: One entry per venue you want to compare: 2 to 5 total, all in this one call (a Kalshi ticker and a Polymarket slug for the same bet are two entries). Each must genuinely be the same real-world bet; this tool does not verify that for you.

tools.name: workflow.run_cross_venue_arbitrage
tools.title: Cross Venue Arbitrage
tools.description: Checks 2-5 quotes for the SAME real-world binary bet across venues (or manually-supplied probabilities) for a direction-independent price gap at the quoted prices: "Yes" at whichever venue quotes it cheapest, "No" at whichever venue quotes "Yes" most expensively (its own "No" price is assumed to be 1 minus its own "Yes" price, the standard complementary-binary convention). Reports isArbitrage, the cost to lock in $1 of guaranteed payout, the locked-in profit and ROI at the quoted prices for a given stake, and which venue quotes each side. feePctPerLeg is an optional per-leg trading-fee rate that can and does erase a real-looking spread - reported honestly via isArbitrage rather than always showing a positive number. Use when user asks "can I arbitrage this bet across venues?" or "does the quoted price gap survive fees?". The caller asserts the venues quote the same bet; this tool does not verify that. If available is false, do not use any result field (computed figures and any verdict are null or empty), so read available first.

venue.description: Prediction-market venue this quote comes from

identifier.description: Kalshi ticker, Polymarket slug, ADI Predictstreet symbol, Limitless slug, or Myriad slug, matching the venue field.

quotes.description: Live mode: one entry per venue, 2-5 total. Provide this OR manualProbabilitiesPct, not both.

manualProbabilitiesPct.description: Manual mode: 2-5 probabilities (0.01-99.99) already known for the same bet across different venues, when you don't want a live fetch. Provide this OR quotes, not both.

stakeUsd.description: Total capital to deploy across both legs

feePctPerLeg.description: Optional per-leg trading-fee rate, e.g. 0.02 for 2% (default 0)

tools.name: workflow.run_market_implied_odds
tools.title: Market Implied Odds
tools.description: Reads Kalshi's full live BTC or ETH year-end price ladder (a set of mutually-exclusive prediction markets covering the whole price range) and reports what the market itself implies: the median (50th-percentile) price bucket, the single most-likely (mode) bucket, and the probability of ending the year at or above any real bucket boundary. Deliberately does not compute an expected value or interpolate inside a bucket: the top/bottom buckets are open-ended, so any point estimate there would need an invented assumption; every number this tool returns traces back to one live, sourced price. Use when user asks "what does the market think BTC will be worth by year end?" or "what are the odds ETH ends the year above $X?". Returns: buckets[] (label, floor, cap, probabilityPct), medianBucketLabel, modeBucketLabel, vigPct, probabilityAtOrAbovePct + snappedThresholdUsd (only when thresholdUsd is supplied). If available is false, do not use any result field (computed figures and any verdict are null or empty), so read available first.

coin.description: Which coin's year-end ladder to read. Default BTC.

thresholdUsd.description: Optional price threshold: returns the probability of ending the year at or above the nearest real bucket boundary at or below this value.

tools.name: workflow.run_black_scholes_live
tools.title: Black-Scholes Option Price and Greeks (Live)
tools.description: Black-Scholes theoretical price and Greeks for a REAL, live option instrument on Deribit (BTC/ETH, coin-settled) Binance (BTC, ETH, XAU, XAG, USDT-settled) or Bybit (BTC, ETH, USDT-settled): pulls that instrument's own spot, strike, days to expiry, and implied volatility from the venue, then reports how far the venue's actual quoted mark price sits from what Black-Scholes implies at that IV (priceDiscrepancyPct). This is the trust-check tool: "is this exchange's quoted price consistent with its own volatility assumption?", not an estimate, a live formula cross-check. Use when user gives a specific instrument name (e.g. "BTC-27FEB27-90000-C" on Deribit, "BTC-261225-90000-C" on Binance, "BTC-25DEC26-90000-C-USDT" on Bybit) and asks "is this option fairly priced?" or "what are the Greeks on this contract?". Returns everything workflow.run_black_scholes does, plus instrumentName, exchange, premiumCurrency (BTC/ETH for Deribit, USDT for Binance and Bybit), optionType, markPrice, markIvPct, bsPrice, priceDiscrepancyPct, available (false + error if the instrument name doesn't resolve, the contract has expired or has no IV quote, a Binance contract states no usable risk-free rate (missing or outside -100 to 100%), or a Binance or Bybit market is not trading; then do not use any result field, they are null; read available first). For Deribit also currency, deribitMarkPriceCoin, deribitMarkIvPct, bsPriceCoin; for Binance and Bybit those and the coin-quoted callPriceCoin/putPriceCoin are null (prices are in USDT per unit, delta, gamma, vega, theta and rho are the standard USD ones for both). A contract whose mark is only a cent or two can show a large priceDiscrepancyPct; read the absolute gap there. The rate Binance states can be negative; it is returned as riskFreeRatePct, and workflow.run_black_scholes accepts 0 to 100 only, so a negative one cannot be fed back into it. Bybit prices off the forward of the expiry and states no rate: for Bybit `spot` is that forward (indexPrice is the venue index when it quotes one), riskFreeRatePct is 0, delta and gamma are per unit of the forward, and rhoCallPerPct/rhoPutPerPct are null for Bybit only (there is no rate to differentiate), the one field of workflow.run_black_scholes it does not return as a number.

instrumentName.description: Exact instrument name: Deribit BTC-27FEB27-90000-C, Binance BTC-261225-90000-C (expiry YYMMDD), Bybit BTC-25DEC26-90000-C-USDT (expiry DMMMYY). Get one from the venue's options chain; this tool does not browse the chain, it prices one named instrument.

exchange.description: Venue of the instrument. Default deribit.

riskFreeRatePct.description: Risk-free rate in percentage points, Deribit only. Default 0: standard crypto-options convention. Binance states its own rate for each contract and the price uses that one; a value here is not used for Binance or Bybit (Bybit: the forward is the base, rate 0).

tools.name: workflow.run_forex_correlation_live
tools.title: Forex Correlation (Live)
tools.description: Correlation coefficient and minimum-variance hedge ratio between two forex pairs, fetched live: historical daily rates for both pairs over the given lookback window (frankfurter.app's daily ECB reference time series, business days only), aligned by matching date, computed on daily % returns. hedgeRatio follows Hull's standard futures-hedging formula: "how many units of pair2 per unit of pair1 minimizes the combined position's variance." Use when user asks "how correlated are EUR/USD and GBP/USD?" or "what hedge ratio should I use between these two pairs?". Returns: n (overlapping trading days used), correlation (-1 to 1), hedgeRatio, available (false + error if either pair has no data, or too few dates overlap). If available is false, do not use any result field (computed figures and any verdict are null or empty), so read available first.

tools.name: workflow.run_price_consensus
tools.title: Price Consensus
tools.description: Cross-exchange agreement check for one perpetual futures price: fetches the same asset USDT/USDC-margined perpetual from a reference set of 7 liquid exchanges (Binance, Bybit, OKX, Gate, KuCoin, Hyperliquid, MEXC; the chosen one is compared against the rest) and reports the median of the others, the spread across all, and how far the chosen exchange sits from that median. Says the exchanges disagree instead of guessing: status is agree (under 0.25%), warn (0.25% to 1%), diverge (1% or more) or insufficient (fewer than 3 other exchanges returned a comparable contract; inverse, dated and unlisted contracts are not compared, and that is not a verdict on the price). Use before acting on a live price: "is this Bybit BTC price in line with the market?" Symbol is the perp symbol as that exchange names it (e.g. BTCUSDT on bybit, ETH-USDT-SWAP on okx). Returns: status, summary, median, peerMedian, spreadPct, deviationPct, sources, quotes (price per exchange), thresholds_pct, as_of.

exchange.description: Exchange code of the price being checked, e.g. bybit, binance, okx, gate, kucoin, hyperliquid, mexc

symbol.description: That exchange's own perpetual symbol, e.g. BTCUSDT (bybit/binance), ETH-USDT-SWAP (okx), BTCUSDC (hyperliquid)

tools.name: workflow.run_prediction_market_edge
tools.title: Prediction Market Edge
tools.description: Compares your own probability estimate for an event against a prediction market's price (manual entry, or a live Kalshi ticker, Limitless slug, or Myriad slug) and sizes a bet using fractional Kelly criterion bet sizing (default: quarter-Kelly, a standard conservative haircut on full Kelly, stated explicitly as a convention). Returns a zero Kelly stake whenever your probability doesn't exceed the market's price: no edge. Use when user asks "does this bet have edge?" or "what does Kelly sizing give for my probability estimate against the market's price?". Provide exactly one of marketProbabilityPct/kalshiTicker/limitlessSlug/myriadSlug. Returns: edgePct, evPerDollarStaked, fullKellyFraction, cappedKellyFraction, recommendedStakeUsd, verdict (a label for the size of cappedKellyFraction: skip_this_one/think_twice/worth_the_risk/take_it, not a recommendation). If available is false, do not use any result field (computed figures and any verdict are null or empty), so read available first.

marketProbabilityPct.description: The market's probability (price), 0.01-99.99. Use this OR one of the live sources below, not both.

kalshiTicker.description: A Kalshi market ticker to fetch the market probability from live instead of supplying it manually.

limitlessSlug.description: A Limitless Exchange market slug to fetch the market probability from live instead of supplying it manually.

myriadSlug.description: A Myriad Markets market slug to fetch the market probability from live instead of supplying it manually. Not every market has a Yes/No outcome.

bankrollUsd.description: Bankroll available for this bet, in USD

kellyFractionCap.description: Fraction of full Kelly to actually stake, 0.01-1. Default 0.25 (quarter-Kelly).
